instructions.caption:
We talk a lot about the "Strong Woman" trope. The woman who holds the family together, works the job, serves at the church, and never complains. But what happens when that strength runs out?

On this week's Sacrificial Conversations, Tammy gave us a chillingly accurate description of ultimate burnout. She described sitting outside on the floor, having an out-of-body experience, watching herself scream in a parking lot. When her mother told her to just "take a deep breath," she realized she couldn't. Because exhaling just meant making room for 80 more stressful things to rush back in.

If your life feels like a "choke" right now, Teddy and Monica want you to know this: God did not build you to carry the weight of the world. It is okay to put it down. instructions.caption:
Have you ever thought about what would happen if there was no more YOU?

We spend so much of our lives pouring out for our families, our churches, our jobs, and our friends. But here is a hard, biblical truth we unpacked on the Sacrificial Conversations podcast this week: You can pray all day for strength, but God also gave you common sense to rest. When your cup is completely empty, your health will eventually force you to stop.

Sometimes, the greatest sacrifice you can make is your own pride and your need to be a people-pleaser. Saying "NO" is not a sin. In fact, "No" is a complete sentence. If you are running on fumes today, this is your sign to stop, breathe, and prioritize the vessel God gave you.

Catch the rest of this powerful conversation with Teddy & Monica. Listen to us live every Monday on WFTB 104.1 TabNashville, or watch the full episode here: [YouTube Link]
